title: The press says the human brain finally has a rival.
description:
The press says the human brain finally has a rival. The New Yorker called the Perceptron 'the first serious rival to the human brain ever devised'. The New York Times ran the headline 'New Navy Device Learns By Doing'.

A Cornell psychologist. His Perceptron ran on a five-ton IBM 704, and after 50 trials it taught itself to tell a card marked on the left from one marked on the right. He called it 'the first machine capable of having an original idea'.

It could not tell whether two inputs disagreed. In 1969 Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert proved a single-layer perceptron cannot compute XOR, one of the simplest logic functions there is. Rosenblatt's machine had one layer. Today's networks have millions.

An AI winter set in. Funding for neural networks dried up, and the field turned elsewhere for years. Rosenblatt did not see the thaw: he drowned in 1971, sailing, on his forty-third birthday.

The machine that would rival the brain had been on the right track all along, about sixty years too soon.

Sources:
- https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2019/09/professors-perceptron-paved-way-ai-60-years-too-soon (Cornell Chronicle, Melanie Lefkowitz, 25 September 2019; read in full 27 August 2026): established that in July 1958 the US Office of Naval Research demonstrated Frank Rosenblatt's Perceptron on a five-ton, room-sized IBM 704, which after 50 trials taught itself to tell cards marked on the left from cards marked on the right; that Rosenblatt, a research psychologist at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory, called it 'the first machine which is capable of having an original idea'; that the New York Times headline read 'NEW NAVY DEVICE LEARNS BY DOING: Psychologist Shows Embryo of Computer Designed to Read and Grow Wiser' and the New Yorker called it 'the first serious rival to the human brain ever devised'; that the perceptron had a single layer while modern networks have millions; that its rise and fall helped usher in the 'AI winter'; that Rosenblatt drowned in 1971 on his 43rd birthday; and that his Mark I perceptron now sits in the Smithsonian.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perceptrons_(book) (Wikipedia, 'Perceptrons (book)'; read in full 27 August 2026): established that Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert published Perceptrons in 1969; that its proofs showed a single-layer perceptron cannot compute certain simple predicates including the XOR function; that the book is commonly credited with helping shift AI funding toward symbolic systems and contributing to the AI winter; and, as a complicating point, that this causal story is contested, with Minsky and Papert themselves later saying research waned for other reasons and critics such as Bernard Widrow calling the proofs largely irrelevant.
